# bugs #4155: mcs51: warning 127 for a cast from uintptr_t to a generic pointer

- Ticket: https://sourceforge.net/p/sdcc/bugs/4155/
- Category: [Fixes that need a decision](../../fix-decision.md)
- Evidence: tested on r17176
- Recommended action: Confirm the two choices under Decision, then apply the patch and close.
- Patch: [bugs-4155.patch](../../patches/bugs-4155.patch). Applies to r17176 without the other patches.
<!-- end of generated block -->

## Finding

For mcs51, sdcc r17158 gives warning 127, "non-pointer type cast to generic pointer", for
`(void *)i` when `i` is a `uintptr_t`. On mcs51, `uintptr_t` is `unsigned long` with 4 bytes, and
a generic pointer has 3 bytes. The cast was compiled for mcs51 only.

## Cause

`checkPtrCast` in `src/SDCCast.c` has a branch for conversions from an integer to a generic object
pointer on the ports where `GPTRSIZE > FARPTRSIZE`. The branch gives warning 88 for a nonzero
literal and warning 127 for every other integer. It does not test the size of the integer type.

## Fix

The branch gives warning 127 only when the integer type is smaller than a generic pointer. For an
integer type of at least that size, a cast gets no diagnostic, and a conversion without a cast
gets warning 154, "converting integral to pointer without a cast". Warning 88 for nonzero literals
is unchanged.

## Decision

The limit is the size of the type in bytes. On mcs51 the patch therefore removes the warning for
casts from `long` and `long long` as well as from `uintptr_t` and `intptr_t`. Integers of these
types supply all three bytes of the pointer, including the byte with the memory tag. The patch
attached to the first comment counts bits with `bitsForType` where this patch counts bytes with
`getSize`. By the code the two differ for `_BitInt` types of 17 to 23 bits, which occupy three
bytes. Only the patch from the first comment keeps warning 127 for them. The ticket names a second
option, which is to keep the warning and to remove the comment from the regression test.

A conversion without a cast from such an integer, as in `return u;` in a function that returns
`void *`, gets warning 154 with the patch. Trunk gives warning 127 for it. By its code, the patch
attached to the first comment gives no diagnostic for this conversion, because `checkPtrCast`
tests for warning 154 only outside the branch for generic pointers. That patch was not compiled.

## Verification

`support/valdiag/tests/bug-4155.c` has four cases. `TEST1` is the cast from the ticket, and `TEST2`
converts a pointer to `uintptr_t` and back. Neither may produce a diagnostic. `TEST3` must produce
a warning on mcs51 for a cast from `unsigned char`. `TEST4` must produce a warning on every port
for the conversion without a cast. Without the change to `SDCCast.c`, `TEST1` gets warning 127 on
mcs51. With the patch, the comment in `mm-pnvi-ae-udi-pointer_from_int_disambiguation_2_xy.c` that
the ticket cites describes what sdcc does.
